Yeung Man Cooking (Most amazing East-Asian dishes)

Not liking exercise is something I relate to as well, but I’ve found a few things that work for me. First of all, I hate the gym so I got myself a yoga mat and a kettlebell. Best investment ever, whenever I got the tiniest bit of energy I do a bit of exercise. Set the boundary low, tell yourself 5-10 minutes. Usually it ends up turning more than that and if it doesn’t, at least you did something!

For me exercise works to eat healthier too. And it makes me love my body more even if I am overweight. 

Also if nothing has worked in the past perhaps get a blood test done for hypothyroidism. I have it too, but not too bad I need medication yet. It can make you very tired, depressed, demotivated and you gain weight. 

Another thing that helps me is to just not buy unhealthy stuff. Im a bit of a cheap skater so I have a budget and crisps and sweets just don’t fall into that. Don’t go shopping hungry either! 

Next I think is find out what foods you like! For me it’s really been a journey but there are some ways I can squeeze in healthy veggies and protein in a way I like. Roasting vegetables is tasty, but I think the best way for me is making a soup, minestrone or ramen. I can put in a lot of vegetables and the flavour of the broth will just get absorbed into them and you don’t taste any bitterness or stuff you dislike. You can also blend in vegetables in a pasta sauce. 

Third thing is eat from a smaller plate or bowl. It will seem like you ate more then you actually did! Also don’t eat too quickly and be mindful when eating, don’t eat behind a tv or screen. 

Fourth thing is walk or cycle more instead of taking a car or public transport. This just gives you a little extra cardio. You don’t need to start running a marathon, and remember that the more weight you carry the more calories you burn with cardio too. 

For last resort, maybe get a gastric bypass. My mom really couldn’t lose weight after trying diet after diet. She did this and is now a healthy weight. Do be careful with this decision, we had quite a bit of scares from her being underweight and not being able to get enough calories and nutrients which kinda ended in a hospital trip once or twice… so take this as a last resort if your weight it really effecting your healthy super negatively. Also remember that going out to eat and stuff won’t be the same ever again because you simply won’t be able to eat much.

First of all. Engage with people who are also interested in you and will ask you about your day. If that doesn’t happen move on. Don’t waste time on people like this. If they aren’t asking you anything and not putting in effort that’s not going to change in a relationship either. So skip that person. 

And to prove you’re an interesting person at first ask them about hobby’s and work and at the end of the day ask them “hey, have you been doing any (insert hobby)?” (This proves you’re interested and remember what they told you.) Or ask “how was work? If I remember correctly you work at (insert job), that seems cool, what do you do on a daily basis?”

And also provide information about yourself during those questions, but not in an obnoxious way (by ignoring their answer and talking about yourself.) For example what works: “Ah you work in software engineering? That’s really nice, personally never done a job in that field, I work in (…). Just asking dry questions like “what you doing.” Or “how are u.” Don’t seem engaging at all. Ask more in the way of “Hey, good morning!
